newsitem.title: GERMANY: German exchanges to unify DAX prices from July 31.
newsitem.headline: German exchanges to unify DAX prices from July 31.

text.p: Seven of Germany's eight regional stock exchanges will harmonise prices for the 30 shares on the blue chip DAX index in floor trading from July 31, Deutsche Boerse AG said on Tuesday.
Harmonised prices have been available since July 21 for the 70 shares on the MDAX mid-cap index but technical complications delayed the inclusion of the top-traded shares until this week.
The new system will provide harmonised opening and closing prices for DAX stocks and also a single price at the "Kassa", or mid-bourse pricing point.

The participating bourses are Frankfurt, which is by far the largest, as well as Munich, Duesseldorf, Hanover, Hamburg, Stuttgart and Berlin. Previously, arbitrage was theoretically possible between prices on these exchanges.
Bremen, the eighth regional exchange, declined to take part.
